description: Team AlphaMatrix from Bangladesh. We're building: NASA-ISRO NISAR radar sees through monsoon clouds to forecast riverbank erosion and catch sinking flood embankments before they breach, then warns families by SMS in Bangla. We cover full-stack, AI/ML, backend/APIs, IoT, geography, and storytelling. Seeking SAR/InSAR, GIS, hydrology, or UI/UX skills. Brand-new data, a real problem, a working system in 48 hours. Join us!
summary: NodiNajar (নদীনজর, "River Watch") is an open-source web app that uses NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar to track riverbank erosion on the Jamuna River in Sirajganj, Bangladesh. Erosion peaks in the monsoon, when clouds hide the ground from optical satellites, so families get no warning. NISAR sees through cloud and rain. NodiNajar reads eight NISAR L2 GCOV passes (June to September 2026), maps water and land on each pass, follows only the outer banks, and measures how far each 500 m stretch moved and how many homes now stand near the edge. It answers "Dancing with the SARs" with a pass player, a before/after swipe, HH and HV comparison, optical context from NASA GIBS and HLS, a check against NASA OPERA (94 to 96% agreement), and hypotheses on the drivers. High-risk stretches turn into Bangla SMS and voice alerts and a priority list for officials. It matters because about a million people in Bangladesh are affected by riverbank erosion, and NISAR can now give them a fresh warning every 12 days.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NodiNajar turns NASA-ISRO NISAR radar into a riverbank erosion warning for the Jamuna River in Sirajganj, Bangladesh. It shows where the bank moved, by how much, how many homes stand near the new edge, and who to warn first.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: eight NISAR L2 GCOV passes (18 Jun to 22 Sep 2026, track 69, frame 14, provisional) from NASA's Alaska Satellite Facility DAAC. Our code reads only our 80 km box from each file.

2. Water and land: in HH polarization, water is dark and land is bright. We threshold each pass into a water mask. Water area rose from 454 km² on 18 Jun to 967 km² on 24 Jul.

3. Erosion, not flooding: flooded sandbars are not erosion, so we track only the outer banks, cut into 500 m stretches, and measure how far each moved from the first pass.

4. People at risk: homes within 200 m of the new bank, from Overture Maps buildings. 38 stretches moved and 5 are next to homes. One west-bank stretch moved 160 m, with 67 homes now within 200 m.

5. Alerts: a fixed Bangla template filled with measured numbers, for SMS and voice, plus a priority list for officials. Sending is switched off in this demo.

HOW IT ANSWERS THE CHALLENGE

- Interactive NISAR app: pass player, before/after swipe, 3D view, stretch list.

- Surface change over time: bank retreat, floodplain filling and draining, channel shifts.

- Polarizations: HH for water and land, HV for vegetation on char islands, side by side.

- Other data for context: NASA GIBS VIIRS daily imagery (the cloud that hides the banks), HLS optical swipe, NASA POWER rainfall.

- Physical and human drivers: a "Why it moves" page with hypotheses (loose silt banks, a braided channel, falling water, sand dredging, bank protection), each with a source.

- Future uses of NISAR: 12-day warnings, embankment movement from interferometry, char-island tracking.

DOES IT WORK? WE TESTED IT

- Forecast: we hid the last two passes and forecast them. Typical error: 17 m (median of 56 checks), 10 m on high-risk stretches. Only 59% of results fell inside our forecast range against an 80% target, so the range is still too narrow.

- NASA OPERA DSWx-HLS: our NISAR water maps agreed with OPERA on 94.1% (29 Aug) and 96.0% (10 Sep) of comparable cells.

- News back-test: of 16 erosion reports from this monsoon, 2 fall on banks we measure. One was flagged 23 days before the report, one only after. 6 were on char islands, which version 1 does not track, and 8 could not be placed precisely.

- Honest limit: on pass pairs with similar water levels, the measured bank still moved about 20 m, so part of the season totals may reflect water level. The app says so.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Families near an eroding bank get days of warning to move belongings and livestock. Upazila officials and the Water Development Board get a ranked list of where to act. Every result is labelled provisional and traceable to open code.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

Python (h5py, NumPy, SciPy, pyproj, Pillow, pytest) for the radar pipeline, with 57 unit tests. TypeScript with Next.js, React, MapLibre GL, deck.gl and Recharts for the web app, hosted as a static site on Vercel. FFmpeg and Playwright for the videos.

WHAT'S NEXT

A char-island engine, a warning with every new NISAR pass, embankment movement from NISAR GUNW interferometry, water-level correction, a real SMS and voice gateway through union parishads, and a second river (the Teesta).

USE OF AI

Claude (Anthropic) helped research, write code and tests, draft text and scripts, and edit the videos. ElevenLabs generated the narration voice from our script; this is stated in the video credits, descriptions and file metadata. No AI computes any number in the app; every figure comes from deterministic, tested code. No AI writes the alerts. Full log: https://github.com/Anthony-Kishan/NodiNajar/blob/main/docs/AI_USE.md

PRIOR WORK

Work started in October 2026, before the hackathon. We disclosed this to our Local Lead, who allowed it.

Code (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/Anthony-Kishan/NodiNajar
